claims.quote: the draft model predicts likely verification outcomes and pre-speculates tokens for those outcomes in advance
claims.claim: The feature request describes the asynchronous speculation mechanism.
claims.conditions: A predicted outcome must match the actual verification result for the next speculation to be ready immediately.
claims.reported_result: The issue repeats a paper claim of up to 2× speedup over optimized speculative decoding; it reports no vLLM measurement.
claims.transfer_inference: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash could benefit if drafting latency is material and likely outcomes can be predicted cheaply.
claims.limitations: B200 performance, outcome prediction accuracy, draft cost, and any measured vLLM bottleneck are unknown. The issue is closed as not planned; its supplied text gives no technical reason.

claims.quote: If the actual verification outcome is in the predicted set, a speculation can be returned immediately
claims.claim: The paper states the conditional latency benefit of preparing branches during verification.
claims.conditions: The actual outcome must be among the prepared branches.
claims.reported_result: The supplied conclusion claims Saguaro is on average 30% faster than its strongest speculative decoding baselines.
claims.transfer_inference: The mechanism is relevant to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash only if verification and branch preparation can overlap in its serving configuration.
claims.limitations: The supplied excerpt omits experiment configurations and implementation details. B200 hardware, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash results, resource quantities, and effect size on this target are unknown.

claims.claim: The paper identifies cached speculation and additional draft devices as resources that can reduce latency.
claims.conditions: Scaling the number of draft devices increases the speculation cache; the authors say returns eventually diminish.
claims.reported_result: The supplied excerpt gives no device count, cache size, or cost for the proposed transfer.
claims.transfer_inference: Any B200 evaluation must account for extra draft compute, memory, and hardware when comparing latency and throughput.
claims.limitations: The magnitude of those costs for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is unknown.

claims.claim: The authors caution that speculative decoding adds verification work to compute-bound serving.
claims.conditions: The caution applies to throughput-bound workloads such as large-scale RL and offline data generation.
claims.reported_result: The conclusion also claims a better latency-throughput frontier for SSD after accounting for additional hardware, without supplying measurements in this excerpt.
claims.transfer_inference: A throughput-bound DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash deployment may have less to gain than a latency-bound one.
claims.limitations: Whether the proposed vLLM workload is throughput-bound is unknown; no measured vLLM bottleneck is supplied.

claims.quote: Full sweep run 38438383633 passed all 17 points and both evals
claims.claim: The PR reports validation of B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe settings.
claims.conditions: The documented settings vary by DEP configuration and concurrency; the PR changes guide text only.
claims.reported_result: The author reports 17 sweep points and two evaluations passed.
claims.transfer_inference: These configurations provide relevant baselines for a B200 experiment.
claims.limitations: The PR reports no asynchronous speculation implementation, bottleneck measurement, or speedup. Workload details and effect size for SSD are unknown.

claims.quote: Preemption frees the request's KV state and resets its computed-token state, making that late output stale.
claims.claim: The open PR describes a correctness hazard when asynchronous speculative output arrives after preemption.
claims.conditions: Its proposed handling discards stale output after preemption and counts each speculative frame as 1 + num_scheduled_spec placeholder tokens, including across repeated preemptions.
claims.reported_result: The source lists regression tests to add and a test command, but no completed test result.
claims.transfer_inference: An SSD integration needs explicit in-flight output invalidation and KV-state accounting across preemption and prefix-cache reset.
claims.limitations: This is a proposed vLLM fix, not evidence that the same path is implemented or validated for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on B200.

claims.claim: A separate vLLM asynchronous DP-coordination PR reports a modest measured TPOT improvement.
claims.conditions: The benchmark uses DeepSeek-R1 with MTP, DP8, expert parallelism, and 2048 maximum request concurrency; the PR is closed and unmerged.
claims.reported_result: The supplied tables report mean TPOT falling by 7.30 ms, while mean TTFT rises from 20707.70 to 24249.12 ms.
claims.transfer_inference: Async scheduling can expose overlap opportunities, but this result cannot establish an SSD benefit for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
claims.limitations: Hardware is unknown. The model, workload, and mechanism differ; the result measures DP coordination, not asynchronous speculation.

claims.quote: max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens) tokens per sequence-parallel rank
claims.claim: A separate open PR specifies a decode workspace whose capacity grows with speculative token count.
claims.conditions: The stated workspace applies to the PR's FlashInfer MegaMoE path; the reported throughput benchmark uses Beam prefill on GB300.
claims.reported_result: The PR reports 168.8K versus 98.7K input tokens/s for Beam prefill, unrelated to SSD.
claims.transfer_inference: Speculation depth can affect serving memory and warmup costs, so a B200 experiment should measure these costs.
claims.limitations: The formula and Beam result do not quantify SSD's extra branch cache or its DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash effect.

claims.quote: both models to perform predictions independently on separate devices
claims.claim: The AMUSD abstract proposes asynchronous drafting and verification with separate devices.
claims.conditions: The design assumes independently running draft and verify models.
claims.reported_result: The abstract claims an average 29% improvement over speculative decoding and identical output quality.
claims.transfer_inference: Separate devices are one possible way to overlap work for the target deployment.
claims.limitations: This is an abstract, not implementation evidence. Hardware, workload, resource cost, correctness method, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash effect are unknown.

claims.claim: The SwiftSpec abstract identifies correctness and communication obstacles to asynchronous speculative decoding.
claims.conditions: Its stated setting is small-batch tensor-parallel low-latency decoding.
claims.reported_result: The abstract claims an average 1.75× speedup across five model families and six datasets and cites a Llama3-70B result on eight Hopper GPUs.
claims.transfer_inference: A B200 transfer must check KV consistency and communication costs under the actual DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash parallelism and batch sizes.
claims.limitations: This is an abstract, not implementation evidence. It supplies no DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash or B200 result.
